description:
FILED s540b (Opus 5.5, 2026-11-13), docs/speed-low-hanging-review-s540.md THE LIST #1.  Code sha 05806e16.

WHERE: cl/pcl-runtime.lisp `do-tr` (~line 42116).  The op struct (p-tr-op) is already built ONCE per site (%p-op-once, #1250), but do-tr calls expand-tr-chars on from and to, builds a fresh EQL hash table from-set, and for a complement (/c) op runs (sort (remove-duplicates (map 'vector #'char-code from-chars)) #'<) -- remove-duplicates on a vector is O(n^2) with EQL, so `tr/\0-\377//c` (Data::Dumper's `_dump`, line 587: `$val =~ tr/\0-\377//c` for EVERY dumped value) costs 65,000 comparisons per call.  A count-only tr (empty replacement, no /d /s: perl's OPpTRANS_IDENTICAL) still builds the whole result string with with-output-to-string just to count.

MEASUREMENT (scratch/s540b/lev/tr-cache.lisp redefines do-tr: the expansion + from-set + sorted complement list cached per op in an EQ table keyed on the op, the sorted list built from the hash keys, and the identical case counting without building a string; ab.pl --lever, interleaved best of 5, base-vs-base C/A beside it; legs/leg1.log, quiet box load 1.1-1.4):
  dumper  (Data::Dumper, 300 records x 10 dumps)   7.120 -> 0.591 s  -91.7 %  (C/A +0.1 %)
  podtext (Pod::Text over perlfunc.pod)            0.809 -> 0.678 s  -16.2 %  (C/A -0.7 %)
  tbal    (Text::Balanced)                         0.111 -> 0.107 s   -3.1 %  (C/A -0.1 %)
Profile before (sb-sprof): do-tr 77 % cumulative of dumper, vector-remove-duplicates* 65 %.  decode_base64 of a 16-char string is 22 us under PCL (perl XS 0.05) for the same reason (`tr{A-Za-z0-9+/=}{}cd` in MIME::Base64's shim).
Prevalence: 746 `=~ tr` / `=~ y` sites in 383 files over perl's lib + ~/.cpan/build + everyday.

THE FIX (one function, runtime only, no emission change): add a slot to p-tr-op (or a lazily filled `compiled` slot like p-regex-op's %compiled) holding from-chars, to-chars, the from-set table and the sorted complement vector, filled on first use; build the sorted vector from the table's keys (or a 0..255 bitmap for the common Latin-1 case); for the identical case return the count without building the result.  The op is per site and immutable once built, so the cache needs no validity test.  A NON-literal op (built per call) pays what it pays today.

BAR: `prove Pl/t/` files naming tr (grep -l 'tr/' Pl/t) + the full gate; the sweep (tr.t is in perl-tests: 241 rows -- must stay +0); everyday; the three rows above reproduced on a quiet box.  Inverse: the guard rows already exist (tr.t, the #4264 identical/read-only rows, the #1493 count-only-on-a-reference row) -- re-read #4264's rule (an identical tr never writes its target) and keep it.

DO NOT: key a cache on the op's TEXT across sites (two sites may differ in modifiers); do not drop the read-only die for a non-identical tr on a raw string (`%p-readonly-modification` arm).

=== s540 (2026-11-13) === scheduled: s540/s540d-prompt.md (the USER: the speed fixing is a normal task).
subject: PERF (s540b, measured): `tr///` re-expands its search/replacement lists, rebuilds a hash table and -- under /c -- runs an O(n^2) remove-duplicates on EVERY call; Data::Dumper programs are 12x slower than they need to be (dumper.pl 7.12 -> 0.59 s with a cached op)
